nodes.name: Question 2.11
nodes.statement:
Given $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ with positive upper Banach density, does there exist an infinite set $B \subset\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists a shift $t_k\geq0$ with
\[\left\{ \sum_{n \in F}  n :   F \subset B\textup{ with } 0< |F| \leq k \right\}\subset A-t_k. \]

nodes.name: Conjecture 2.10
nodes.statement: Given $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ with positive upper Banach density, there is an infinite sequence of infinite sets $B_1,B_2, \ldots \subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B_1+\cdots+B_i\subset A$ for every $i\in\mathbb{N}$.

nodes.name: Question 2.12
nodes.statement:
Given $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ with positive upper Banach density, does there exist an infinite set $B \subset\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there is a co-finite set $B'\subset B$ and a shift $t_k\geq0$ with
\[\left\{ \sum_{n \in F}  n :   F \subset B'\textup{ with } 0< |F| \leq k \right\}\subset A-t_k. 
\]

nodes.name: Conjecture 2.4
nodes.statement:
Fix $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
Every set of positive upper Banach density $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ has a shift $A-t$ which contains the set 
\[\left\{ \sum_{n \in F}  n :   F \subset B\textup{ with } 0< |F| \leq k \right\}\]
for some integer $t\ge 0$ and some infinite set $B \subset \mathbb{N}$.

nodes.name: Conjecture 2.9
nodes.statement: Given $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ with positive upper Banach density and $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there are infinite sets $B_1,\dots,B_k\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B_1+\cdots+B_i\subset A$ for all  $i=1,\dots,k$.

nodes.name: Conjecture 2.5
Theorem 2.8
nodes.statement: For every set  $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ of positive upper Banach density and integer $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist infinite sets $B_1, \dots, B_k\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B_1+\cdots+B_k \subset A$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement:
Every set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset
\[t+\big\{ b_1+b_2:b_1,b_2\in B,~b_1\neq b_2 \big\}\]
for some shift $t\geq0$ and some infinite set $B \subset A$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.7
nodes.statement: If $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ has positive upper Banach density, there exist infinite sets $B, C\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+C \subset A$.
